title: Permission definitions
description: Shared permission definitions (F2-02, schema-strategy). NON-NORMATIVE machine artifact: the normative source is spec/core/permissions.md, spec/core/risk-classes.md and spec/glossary.md. A declaration states what a harness can do; declaration is not approval.

scope.description: Reach of a mutation. Project scope limits changes to the target project directory and is the default; user scope touches the global environment and requires an exact preview plus explicit approval. The two scopes MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable. F1: core/permissions.md §1; glossary.md 'Scope'.

riskClass.description: Risk class: A Passive, B Tooling, C Executable, D Privileged. A risk class states what an artifact can do, not that it is safe or trusted. F1: core/risk-classes.md §1, §5.

autonomyLevel.description: Autonomy friction level: 0 Preview, 1 Safe Apply, 2 Trusted Harness, 3 Elevated. The risk class sets the minimum autonomy floor and there MUST NOT be an absolute bypass. F1: glossary.md 'Autonomy level'; core/permissions.md §6.

permission.description: A declared permission. It MUST include the capability it grants, the scope in which it applies and the risk class of the operations it allows. A declared permission does not imply approval. F1: core/permissions.md §2, §3.
The capability contract a declaration grants, drawn from the filesystem, network, execution, tools, models, services, secrets and system axes. F1: core/permissions.md §2.1.

scope.description: The scope in which the permission applies. Project scope is the default. F1: core/permissions.md §1.

riskClass.description: The risk class of the operations the permission allows. F1: core/risk-classes.md §1.

autonomyLevel.description: Optional autonomy level recorded for the permission; it MUST be at least the floor implied by the risk class. F1: core/permissions.md §6.

justification.description: Optional human-readable justification. It is informative and MUST NOT reduce the declared risk class. F1: core/permissions.md §2.4.
